titus.a1: Titus only uses the prices and information you provide; it never quotes a price, promotion or timeframe that isn’t in your profile. When it isn’t sure, it hands the conversation to your team. You see every conversation in the dashboard and can take over anytime.
titus.a2: Titus is your business’s virtual assistant and says so clearly when asked; it never presents itself as a human. You can choose its name. If a customer wants to speak to a person, the conversation goes to your team right away.
titus.a3: No. Titus connects to your existing WhatsApp Business number and Instagram business account. We set up the connection together during onboarding.
titus.a4: No. The Fair Use Shield doesn’t count unnecessary messages, the number of daily replies per person is limited, and you set the monthly budget cap. Once the cap is reached, messages go to your team.
titus.a5: Conversations and leads are stored on our server in Oracle Cloud’s Frankfurt (Germany) data center. To generate a reply, the message is sent to Anthropic; these messages are not used to train the model.
titus.a6: In the demo call, we estimate your monthly cost together based on your business’s message volume. Since the first 300 replies are free, you don’t have to decide before seeing your real usage.
titus.a7: Yes. If your Google Calendar is connected, Titus books the appointment straight into it; if not, it uses the calendar in the dashboard. Your team sees appointments on their phones, and reminders go out automatically either way.
titus.a8: For sectors such as clinics, dentists and hair transplant, clinic mode switches on automatically. In this mode Titus doesn’t quote prices, campaigns or estimated ranges (if you hold a health tourism licence and turn the setting on, it gives prices only to patients writing in a foreign language), doesn’t diagnose, doesn’t recommend treatment, doesn’t ask for health information, tells the patient to call 112 for urgent symptoms, and asks for the patient’s consent before booking. You choose how long conversations are kept. These rules are designed to make it easier to work in line with the regulations; they are not legal advice, and we recommend reviewing your own practice with your legal adviser.

titus.hero.h1: A customer writes at 02:14 a.m. They get an answer at 02:14.

titus.hero.lede: Titus answers the messages your business receives on WhatsApp and Instagram within seconds, in the customer’s own language and with your information. It books appointments into your calendar, sends a reminder the day before and passes what’s needed to the right person on your team.
titus.how.title: It gives your team’s first reply. You make the decisions.
titus.km.data.d: Doesn’t ask for symptoms, complaints, medical history, medication, test results, X-rays or photos. If the patient shares them anyway, it doesn’t repeat or record them; for health questions it hands the conversation to your team.
titus.km.demo: The live demo has two examples: Lina Dental Clinic never quotes prices to anyone. Nova Hair Clinic is a health tourism example; it gives prices to people writing in a foreign language, not to those writing in Turkish.
titus.km.dx.d: Doesn’t diagnose; doesn’t recommend treatments, procedures, medication or doses, and doesn’t promise results. Doesn’t share before-and-after photos, patient reviews or comparisons with other clinics.
titus.km.keep.d: You set in the panel how many days conversations are kept; in clinic mode the default is 365 days. When the period ends, conversations are deleted and appointments stay in the calendar. Your KVKK privacy notice page automatically shows a health-data section and this period.
titus.km.keep.t: You choose how long data is kept
titus.km.lede: If your sector is a clinic, a dentist or hair transplant, clinic mode switches on automatically for a new business and can be set in the panel. While it’s on, Titus follows these rules:
titus.km.legal: Clinic mode is designed to make it easier to work in line with Turkey’s Health Advertising Regulation and KVKK; it is not a substitute for legal advice.
titus.km.note.d: The first automatic message carries the note “I can’t give medical advice; please don’t share your health information here, our specialist team will assess it at your examination.” The note is ready in 48 languages.
titus.km.ok.d: Before booking an appointment it asks the patient for consent to record it and logs the moment consent is given. Without consent no appointment is made, and the patient’s name and phone number aren’t saved either.
titus.km.price.d: Doesn’t give prices, discounts, campaigns, instalments or even an estimated range. It says the fee will be shared by the team after the examination and suggests an appointment; if the customer insists, it hands the conversation to your team.
titus.km.sos.d: For urgent symptoms such as bleeding that won’t stop, swelling, shortness of breath or chest pain, it tells the patient to call 112 and passes the conversation to your team marked “urgent”.
titus.km.title: Stricter rules for clinics.
titus.km.tour.d: If your clinic holds a health tourism licence and you turn this setting on, it gives prices only to patients writing in a language other than Turkish. Patients writing in Turkish don’t get prices.

v1.d: None of our apps ask you to sign up or hand over an email. Open it and go.
v2.d: Our apps have no servers of their own. Your progress, texts and settings are stored on your phone; in Prizma you can also use Google Play Games cloud saves if you like.
v3.d: You win by paying attention, not by guessing. In Lost & Found Office and Prizma, each day’s content is the same for everyone in the world.
v4.d: Our games and apps come in nine or ten languages, English and Turkish among them, and open in your phone’s language.
